Thinking settings

Three models wrote a two-minute drum solo at every thinking setting they offer, at least 4 times each. The 56 solos cost $56 in API fees. They're scored exactly like on the main page, and the gray bands show the middle half of the recorded solos. Every solo is in the grid at the bottom.

These runs use the final prompt from the hill climb on the main page, so they score higher than the same models do on the benchmark prompt. If a program breaks, the error goes back to the model, up to two times. OpenRouter hands each request to one of several providers for a model. Where a model was served by more than one, the marker shape tells you which.

The prompt
Using Python 3 and mido (no other MIDI libraries), write a single script, drum_solo.py, that generates the best two minute drum solo you can as a General MIDI file, solo.mid, on MIDI channel 10. It will be played back on a General MIDI synthesizer.

Make it sound like a great drummer playing:
- Develop motifs: state them, vary them, bring them back, and contrast density and dynamics to build tension and release.
- Let it flow the way a great drummer's hands do: long runs of singles and doubles that travel around the kit, rolls that swell and resolve, fills that carry into the next downbeat.
- Pace it like a showcase solo: keep the energy alive all the way through and land the final hit instead of fading away.
- Shape dynamics inside phrases, with accents, ghost notes and crescendos, more than by making whole sections louder or softer.
- Play it the way a person performs it in real time: the pulse surges and settles with the music, phrases rush ahead or hold back, and notes land where a drummer's hands put them rather than on a quantized grid, with ghost notes against accents.
- Keep inventing: a great soloist rarely plays the same bar twice, even while the motifs stay recognizable.
- Keep it playable by one drummer: at most two hands and two feet striking at any instant.
- The drum kit carries the solo; the rest of the General MIDI percussion set (notes 35–81) is there for color when it serves the music.

Running the script in an empty directory must write solo.mid there, identical on every run. Share drum_solo.py.

Score by reasoning tokens

Length

The prompt asked for two minutes (dotted line), and a solo far from it loses points on the length measurement.

Measures by setting

Each chart is one measure of how a solo is built. The gray band is the middle half of the recorded solos.

Sections

how many distinct sections the solo falls into

Section length

seconds spent in a typical section before moving on

Rhythmic vocabulary

distinct one-beat rhythms in every 64 beats

Reuse

share of beats that repeat a rhythm heard earlier in the solo

Pattern complexity

how compressible the sequence of rhythms is, compared with a shuffled copy, where 1 is as unpredictable as random order

Where the climax falls

the most intense moment (density and loudness together), as a fraction of the way through

Grid lock

how tightly hits sit on a grid of sixteenths and triplets, where 1 is fully quantized

Flow

share of strokes inside steady, even runs

Listen

Every solo, by thinking setting. The square is the solo's structure. Dark blocks on the diagonal are sections, off-diagonal blocks are returns to earlier material. The number is the overall score, then the reasoning tokens spent, and the number of turns when the first reply had no working program.
